verdict.reason: Verified independently. hasCssFetch() (mermaid.ts:368-373) has two branches: raw source and decodeCssEscapes(source). The only source-side CSS test (preview.test.ts:794-807, the sole assertion of 'CSS that loads a URL is not allowed' anywhere in the repo) uses an unescaped `style A background:url("https://evil.example/b.png")`, which the raw-text branch alone catches — removing the decodeCssEscapes disjunct at line 371 would leave the suite green. The escape branch is tested only on the output side (preview.test.ts:480-511, `\75 rl(` / `\40 import` against isSafeCss/CSS_EXTERNAL_RE at mermaid.ts:477-481); a repo-wide grep for `\\75`/`\\40` returns only those engine-output fixtures at lines 488-490. Coverage surface is closed: mermaid.js is imported only by preview.ts:18 and preview.test.ts:14, and preview.test.ts is the only mermaid-touching test in packages/notes, so no counterexample exists elsewhere. Additionally the `@import`, `image-set(` and `cross-fade(` alternatives of CSS_SOURCE_FETCH_RE are never exercised against a fence source (every fence fixture in the file was checked). Blocking under this lens: it is a distinct, mutation-detectable security branch the authors themselves gave a dedicated test on the output side, shipped source-side with a fixture that passes through the other branch.

mergedFrom.summary: Test mutates the real mermaid global config singleton with no teardown

finding.summary: The 'real engine actually honors it' test never touches production code and only round-trips a config echo
finding.evidence: preview.test.ts:631-646 calls `mermaid.initialize({startOnLoad:false, securityLevel:'strict', htmlLabels:false})` with a hardcoded literal and asserts `mermaid.mermaidAPI.getConfig().htmlLabels === false`. It does not import or invoke the code under test (`renderPass`'s initialize call in mermaid.ts:473-479), so if someone renamed, moved (e.g. to `flowchart.htmlLabels`) or deleted the key in mermaid.ts this test still passes — exactly the drift its own comment claims to guard against. It also does not pass `secure: SECURE_KEYS` or `theme`, so the config shape it exercises differs from production. Finally, `getConfig()` echoing a key it was handed does not show the engine *resolves labels* through that key; a mermaid release that kept accepting the key but stopped honouring it in label layout would leave this green while the beacon reopened. The assertion is therefore close to vacuous relative to the stated behavior (upstream honouring the root key), while being presented as the one test covering it.

verdict.reason: The described test does not exist. There is no `getConfig()`/`mermaidAPI.getConfig()` assertion anywhere in packages/notes tests, and no test named "real engine actually honors it" in the repo. preview.test.ts:632-648 (the cited lines) is 'pins htmlLabels per diagram section as well as at the root', which drives production code via `preview.render(DIAGRAM)` and asserts on the recorded `initialize` config — not a hardcoded literal round-trip. The real-engine test at preview.test.ts:708-732 imports and invokes production `renderMermaidBlocks` (mermaid.ts:573, whose initialize call with htmlLabels/flowchart/class/secure/theme is at mermaid.ts:631-640) against real mermaid and asserts outcomes on the engine's serialized layout: `<svg` present, no `foreignObject`, and an actual `svg text` label — so a renamed/moved/dropped key or an engine that stopped honouring it would fail. preview.test.ts:734-748 is the explicit negative control (default htmlLabels, asserts foreignObject IS emitted), the only place a literal `mermaid.initialize({startOnLoad:false, securityLevel:'strict'})` appears, and it is not presented as coverage of the fix. The finding's mechanism (config echo, production code untouched, no outcome assertion) is not present as described.
